summary: Radar for 2026-11-16, all inside the GLP-1 focus. ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov, Washington DC) is the main event. The best fresh hook: Lilly showed full EloraTZP Phase 2 results on 15 Nov, and the trial included a tirzepatide-alone arm. That fits our proven EloraTZP model (fresh randomized data against tirzepatide, shipped within 48 h). It's our biggest earner, so we can also update and link the existing video. Lilly also showed: the SURMOUNT-1/-2 'early responder' analyses, which give the Months 2–6 and Weight Loss long videos a news hook; Zepbound teen data (SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS, −21.4% BMI at 72 weeks); and Foundayo real-world use data. Orforglipron (Foundayo) was also approved in China. The NAION label change is peaking, but mainstream coverage keeps coming (EMJ and Ophthalmology Times, 15 Nov), so it still works as a label-change format and inside 'Serious Risks: How Rare?'. Coverage of stopping is surging (Medscape exit strategies 15 Nov, FOX 5 'rebound risks', Bioengineer). That supports a Keeping Results long video built only from SURMOUNT-4, plus the Cleveland Clinic real-world data, with no switching advice. The Thanksgiving and holiday table is in its last 10 days before the holiday (Prevention, 15 Nov), so it drives the 20:00 Shorts. Evergreen felt-symptom Shorts still lead: injection site, pen, hair, nausea. One correction: REDEFINE 4 (CagriSema vs tirzepatide) came out in February, so it's not a fresh head-to-head. Only REDEFINE 9 (lower doses vs placebo) is new, so we skip it. Rejected: the 'half of users changed their dosing' story (self-titration bait plus cost), black-market and 'research peptide' retatrutide pieces, the CVS $350 pricing stories, and the 'stopping doubles heart attack risk' scare framing.

candidates.topic: EloraTZP vs tirzepatide alone: full Phase 2 results at ObesityWeek (15 Nov 2026): 23.3% average weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight AND type 2 diabetes, plus the dropout numbers (10.8–27% stopped because of side effects on the combination vs 2.9% on tirzepatide alone)
candidates.angle: Fast-turn sequel to our biggest earner: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) vs EloraTZP: Full Results In'. Tell it both ways: more weight loss at the top combination dose, but far more people stopped because of side effects than on tirzepatide alone. Phase 2 and not approved, so we explain what it means for people on tirzepatide today. Update the existing EloraTZP video's pinned comment and link it as 'Watch next'. Population stays exact: overweight or obesity plus type 2 diabetes.
candidates.why_now: Oral session on 15 Nov at ObesityWeek, with financial press (Yahoo Finance '27% dropout') picking it up. Our 10-01 EloraTZP video drew 230+88 searches for these exact terms and 44% of lifetime watch time. Fresh randomized data with a tirzepatide arm is the one news exception the playbook allows.

evidence.signal: EloraTZP Phase 2 oral session 15 Nov; 23.3% (54.1 lb) at 48 weeks; A1C −2.9%
Dropout due to side effects 10.8–27% on the combination vs 2.9% on tirzepatide monotherapy; 27% in the top arm
Population: obesity or overweight plus type 2 diabetes
